clue.text: Whose work once caused feathers to fly?

definitions.text: Whose work once caused feathers to fly?

parts.words: Whose work once caused feathers to fly?
parts.note: an old craftsman who fitted feathers to arrows, so his products sent feathers flying through the air

explanation.surface: Someone stirring up trouble in a bygone age, as in making the feathers fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feathers fly' suggests a row; literally it is fletched arrows in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow-maker who fitted the flights was the traditional trade name for that craftsman.

clue.text: Fail when sick to receive upturn in benefit: stand by this?

indicators.note: to receive means the jumbled word takes something inside it
sick suggests something upset, so the letters are disordered
an upturn in a down clue turns the letters upside down, reading them bottom to top

parts.note: UB, from the UB40 card, stands for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Someone who fails when ill gets a rise in benefit and asks what to rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when sick' rearranges FAIL into FILA; 'upturn' turns UB to BU, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg bone, so something you stand on in a cryptic sense.

clue.text: Players' union with sense of fair play

definitions.meaning: the British trade union for actors and performers
fairness and impartiality, also a body of law based on it

explanation.definitionFit: Equity is both the UK actors' trade union and the principle of fairness.

clue.text: Soldiers needing hospital or to be tucked into bed

indicators.note: tucked into a bed means placed inside it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Wounded soldiers have to go to hospital or be put to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort was a division of a Roman legion, so a body of soldiers.

clue.text: No newts to hold for showing no sign of struggle?

indicators.note: to hold means the first part keeps the second inside it

parts.note: an eft is a newt, so lacking newts is eftless

explanation.surface: A pond with no newts to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Eft is an old word for a newt.
explanation.definitionFit: Done with apparent ease, without visible strain.

clue.text: Pulls your leg when in river

indicators.note: in places the short word inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: Someone playing a practical joke while standing in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull someone's leg is to tease or josh them.

clue.text: Seed packets?

parts.note: eggs are seeds of new life in a sense, and the cardboard cartons that hold them are their packets

explanation.surface: Packets of garden seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardening sense misleads; eggs are the 'seeds', in their cartons.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardboard cartons that hold a half-dozen hen's eggs.

clue.text: Solar radiation's given hustling!

indicators.note: given suggests the letters of the following word are handed over in a different order

explanation.surface: The sun's rays bustling energetically.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from the sun is its visible radiation.

clue.text: Beach wounded to bury English remains

indicators.note: to bury means the outer word encloses the others

parts.note: sore means hurt, wounded
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A wounded man on a beach burying English remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The shore by the sea is the beach.

clue.text: Fox detailed rejection?

parts.note: a fox's tail is its brush, so a fox 'de-tailed' has had its brush taken off; the phrase also means a curt dismissal

explanation.surface: A precise account of why Fox was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as 'thorough' but is de-tailed: the fox's tail, called its brush, removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub or curt dismissal is called a brush-off.

clue.text: Hugo's content with a country

indicators.note: the content of a word is what lies inside its first and last letters

parts.note: and means together with

explanation.surface: Hugo is happy with some unnamed nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'happy' but means the inside of Hugo.
explanation.definitionFit: An East African republic is an example of a country.

clue.text: Well-read try Ariel for a deconstruction

indicators.note: a deconstruction takes the words apart so their letters can be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone well-read tries Ariel, Shakespeare's spirit, in a deconstructionist reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookish person, steeped in books, is literary in taste.

clue.text: Styled as Doctor Petri?

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
a Petri dish is the shallow glass plate used in labs

explanation.surface: Asking whether a doctor called Petri has been given a fashionable look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Petri' looks like a person; it is MO followed by the lab item named after Petri.
explanation.definitionFit: Something styled in the current fashion is fashionable, stylish.

clue.text: Bond secretary with cash and more cash?

parts.note: money is cash
a penny is a further small sum of cash

explanation.surface: James Bond's secretary is paid in cash and more cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Moneypenny is M's secretary in the James Bond stories.

clue.text: Singer: understand her completely

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
to get something is to understand it

explanation.surface: A singer is told: understand her fully.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether and completely are synonyms meaning wholly or entirely.

clue.text: Keeper of royal birds had wrens originally

indicators.note: originally suggests the letters were once in another order and are set right

explanation.surface: The keeper of royal birds once kept wrens.
explanation.definitionFit: Swans in Britain traditionally belong to the Crown, and the keeper of a swannery has this title.

clue.text: Sun destroyed bugs, so peels off

indicators.note: destroyed means the word is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: ticks are parasitic bugs

explanation.surface: The sun kills insects, so something peels away.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstick something is to detach it, pull it free.

clue.text: Daily very French in France!

definitions.note: the definition stands for a place in France

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day
très is French for very

explanation.surface: A newspaper being extremely French while in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper; it is a char, a British cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city south-west of Paris, so a place in that country.

clue.text: City game unfinished in cheerless season

indicators.note: in puts the shortened game inside the season

parts.note: winter is the bleak, cheerless season

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of the game is lopped off

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A city where a game is left unfinished during the bleak months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the last S from CHESS, leaving CHES, which goes inside WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city in Hampshire, England, once the capital of Wessex.

clue.text: Savage rolled up in Lola turbo

indicators.note: rolled up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A savage racer rolling over in a Lola turbo car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled up' in a down clue reads the letters from bottom to top; 'in' points to them sitting inside 'Lola turbo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage and brutal both mean cruelly violent.

clue.text: Burn one hand in scalding vapour

indicators.note: in places the hand inside the vapour

parts.note: steam is scalding vapour
R, for right, is one hand

explanation.surface: Someone burns a hand in hot steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' looks like a scald; it is the Scottish word for a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England a burn is a small brook.

clue.text: Gold one for desperate man to invest, to invest

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: to invest means to surround or besiege, so the man encloses the letter

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strongman character in the British comic The Dandy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A desperate man urged to invest gold and one more sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase does two jobs in turn: first 'to invest' means to besiege (the container), then it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to invest someone with holy orders or official authority.

clue.text: Official without a line

parts.note: not, as in going not having something, stands for without
RY, for railway, is a line

explanation.surface: A functionary who has no line to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal official who certifies documents and witnesses signatures.

clue.text: Round by a hill trader

parts.note: the letter O is round
per means by, as in 'per post'
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A trader has a round of drinks beside a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in markets, someone who does business, is called an operator.

clue.text: Benn's heart, then heart: let's have it again!

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Applause for Benn's spirit, as an audience calls for more.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience cries this when it wants a repeat performance.

clue.text: Person cursed by old woman after three articles

indicators.note: after puts the old woman last

parts.note: an, a and the are the three English articles
ma is a mother, an old woman in slang

explanation.surface: Someone cursed by an elderly lady after reading three newspaper pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema can mean someone or something accursed, excommunicated or loathed.

clue.text: Stay in bustling side-street

indicators.note: bustling suggests busy movement, so the letters jostle into a new order

parts.note: side as written with ST, the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone lodging in a busy side-street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like 'reside' but is the verb 'stop'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay one's hand is to hold back, stop, refrain.

clue.text: Cancel my wild flowers

indicators.note: wild means the letters run riot into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to call off one's wild flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink-flowered plants of the primrose family, whose plural is the same as the singular.
